title: Sheet-Pan Eggs & Sausage
subtitle: Roasted peppers, browned sausage, and baked eggs for a 8–10 person hall breakfast.
description: This firefighter-friendly sheet-pan breakfast roasts peppers and onions beside browned sausage, then bakes eggs right on top. It gives the hall a hot, hearty tray with a short service window and no griddle traffic.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.notes: plus kosher salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika

ingredients.name: shredded cheddar
ingredients.notes: optional, for the last few minutes

ingredients.name: bottle hot sauce
ingredients.notes: and toast or tortillas for the line

steps.title: Heat oven and prep pans
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Line two rimmed half-sheet pans with parchment or foil and oil lightly. Two pans give vegetables room to roast; crowding makes them steam and turn soft.

steps.title: Brown the sausage
steps.instruction: Cook sausage in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it into small crumbles until no pink remains and it reaches 165°F. Drain excess fat, but leave one tablespoon in the pan for flavor.

steps.title: Roast peppers and onions
steps.instruction: Toss peppers and onions with oil, salt, pepper, and smoked paprika. Spread across the pans and roast 12–15 minutes until edges brown. Rotate pans halfway; pale vegetables mean the oven was too cool or the pan was crowded.

steps.title: Add sausage and eggs
steps.instruction: Lower oven to 400°F. Divide sausage over the vegetables, then make 18 small wells and crack in eggs. Keep eggs separated so beginner cooks can portion cleanly; if an egg spills, nudge it back with a spoon before baking.

steps.title: Bake until safely set
steps.instruction: Bake 8–12 minutes until whites are fully opaque and reach 165°F; yolks can stay soft if the crew prefers. Add cheddar for the final 2 minutes. Do not overbake—rubbery yolks are the usual failure mode.

steps.title: Serve or hold for calls
steps.instruction: Serve directly from the sheet pans with toast, tortillas, and hot sauce. For a short call hold, cover loosely and keep at 200°F for up to 15 minutes; uncovered eggs dry out and covered eggs lose roasted texture.

stationWorkflow: Brown sausage while the oven preheats and vegetables roast so the final egg bake is the only last-minute step.
Set one pan at each end of the hall line to prevent a bottleneck when both rigs return at once.
If a call interrupts service, hold at 200°F no longer than 15 minutes; cook a fresh small egg batch if the delay runs longer.
cleanupNotes: Discard parchment or foil after service and soak the sausage skillet immediately to prevent rendered fat from setting.
Wipe egg drips from sheet-pan rims while warm; baked egg protein is much harder to remove cold.
leftovers: Refrigerate portions within 2 hours and reheat sausage and egg portions to 165°F before serving.
Chop cold leftovers into breakfast burrito filling with fresh cheese and salsa.
imageAlt: Sheet-pan breakfast with baked eggs, browned sausage, roasted peppers, and onions

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Confirm corn tortillas are used, or substitute a certified gluten-free wrap.

adaptable.label: Dairy-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a dairy-free cheese shred/block alternative.

adaptable.label: Pork-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Swap in chicken or turkey sausage.
